{{One source|date=January 2024}}

[[File:Nara Sudo-tenno-sha.jpg|280px|thumb|Sudo Tenno Shrine, Nishikidera-cho, Nara City]]
'''Sudo Tenno Shrine''' (崇道天皇神社, ''Sudō Tennō Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} primarily dedicated to {{ill|Prince Sawara|fa|شاهزاده ساوارا|fr|Sawara (prince)|ja|早良親王|ko|사와라 친왕|sh|Princ Sawara|tr|Prens Sawara|zh|早良親王|qid=Q1079634|lt=Prince Sawara}} (Emperor Sudo), found primarily in Nara and across Western Japan{{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=89}}. Alternative names include '''Sudō Tennō-sha''' (崇道天皇社), '''Sudō Jinja''' (崇道神社), and phonetic variations such as '''Sōdō Jinja''' (宗道神社) or '''Sōdo Jinja''' (惣戸神社){{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=89}}.

== History ==
This shrine venerates {{ill|Prince Sawara|fa|شاهزاده ساوارا|fr|Sawara (prince)|ja|早良親王|ko|사와라 친왕|sh|Princ Sawara|tr|Prens Sawara|zh|早良親王|qid=Q1079634|lt=Prince Sawara}}, who died under suspicion of involvement in the assassination of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tanetsugu|fa|فوجیوارا نو تانتسوگو|fr|Fujiwara no Tanetsugu|ja|藤原種継|pt|Fujiwara no Tanetsugu|zh|藤原種繼|qid=Q3090668|lt=Fujiwara no Tanetsugu}}. He passed away during exile in {{ill|Awaji Province|be|Авадзі (правінцыя)|ca|Província d'Awaji|cs|Provincie Awadži|de|Provinz Awaji|es|Provincia de Awaji|fa|ولایت آواجی|fr|Province d'Awaji|id|Provinsi Awaji|it|Awaji (provincia)|ja|淡路国|ko|아와지국|lt|Avadžio žemė|nl|Awaji (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Awaji|pt|Província de Awaji|ru|Авадзи (провинция)|sd|اواجي صوبو|simple|Awaji Province|sk|Awadži (provincia)|sr|Провинција Аваџи|tr|Awaji (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Авадзі|zh|淡路國|zh_min_nan|Awazi-kok|qid=Q1053717|lt=Awaji Province}}, and later was believed to cause calamities. Thus, the shrine has a strong association with the {{ill|Goryō|bcl|Goryō|es|Goryō|fi|Goryō|fr|Goryō|it|Goryō|ja|御霊信仰|ko|어령신앙|no|Goryō|pl|Goryō|sc|Goryō|uk|Ґорьо|zh|御靈信仰|qid=Q3273210|lt=Goryō faith}}. Prince Sawara was reburied at {{ill|Yashima Mausoleum|ja|八島陵|qid=Q24875285}} in Yamato Province, where a shrine named {{ill|Yashima Mausoleum|ja|八島陵|qid=Q24875285}} existed until 1886. Nearby smaller shrines are believed to have branched from it{{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=127}}. The Sudō Tennō-sha in Nishikidera-cho, Nara City, is thought to be established on the former site of the mikoshi hall dedicated to Emperor Sudo during the Nanto Goryō-e (南都御霊会) rituals{{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=126}}<ref>璉珹寺紀</ref><ref>{{ill|Murai Kodō|ja|村井古道|qid=Q96711987}}</ref>.

In regional areas, particularly in the {{ill|San'yō region|ca|San'yō|cs|San’jó|es|Región de San'yō|ff|San'yō region|fr|Région de San'yō|hr|San'yō|ilo|Rehion ti San'yō|ja|山陽地方|ko|산요 지방|pl|Region San’yō|sh|San'yō|simple|San'yō region|sv|Sanyō|th|ซันโย (อนุภูมิภาค)|tl|San'yō|ur|سانیو علاقہ|zh|山陽地方|qid=Q398087|lt=San'yō region}}, the Sudō Jinja or Sōdō shrines may originate from granaries built in 805 (Enryaku 24) by imperial order for the appeasement of Emperor Sudo’s spirit. These granaries later became shrines{{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=120}}<ref name="koki">Nihon Kōki (日本後紀), Enryaku 24</ref><ref name="ruiju">Ruiju Sandai Kyaku (類従三代格)</ref>. These granaries stored 40 bundles of rice annually from each county to appease his spirit{{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=120}}<ref name="koki"/><ref name="ruiju"/>{{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=125}}<ref>Ōkagami</ref><ref>Daianji Sudō Tennō Miin Yashima Ryosho Kibun</ref>.

Some shrines named Sudō Jinja do not enshrine Prince Sawara. For instance, according to the Kōfukuji Kanmu Chōsho (興福寺官務牒疏, 1441), the Sudō Tennō Jinja in Haji, Sōraku County, {{ill|Yamashiro Province|cs|Provincie Jamaširo|de|Provinz Yamashiro|es|Provincia de Yamashiro|fa|ولایت یاماشیرو|fr|Province de Yamashiro|gl|Provincia de Yamashiro|hak|Yamashiro-koet|id|Provinsi Yamashiro|it|Yamashiro (provincia)|ja|山城国|ko|야마시로국|lt|Jamaširo žemė|ms|Yamashiro Province|nl|Yamashiro (provincie)|pt|Província de Yamashiro|ru|Ямасиро (провинция)|simple|Yamashiro Province|sk|Jamaširo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамаширо|tr|Yamashiro (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямашіро|wuu|山城国|zh|山城國|zh_min_nan|Yamasiro-kok|zh_yue|山城國|qid=Q749276|lt=Yamashiro Province}}, venerates {{ill|Prince Toneri|ar|تونيري (الأمير الياباني)|arz|تونى|azb|تونری شاهزاده|ca|Príncep Toneri|de|Toneri-shinnō|es|Príncipe Toneri|eu|Toneri printzea|fa|شاهزاده تونری|fr|Prince Toneri|hu|Toneri herceg|ja|舎人親王|ko|도네리 친왕|pt|Toneri no Miko|zh|舍人親王|zh_yue|舍人 (日本親王)|qid=Q1362200|lt=Prince Toneri}}<ref>Kōfukuji Kanmu Chōsho</ref>{{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=127}}. This may be due to confusion stemming from Prince Toneri’s posthumous title, '''Sudō Jinkei Kōtei''' (崇道尽敬皇帝){{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=127}}.
